question: Which layer of the outer adrenal gland (adrenal cortex) produces stress hormones like cortisol?

options.A: Zona glomerulosa
options.B: Zona reticularis
options.C: Adrenal medulla
options.D: Zona fasciculata

explanation: Think of the adrenal cortex layers from outside in as Salt, Sugar, Sex (Glomerulosa, Fasciculata, Reticularis). The middle layer, zona fasciculata, handles the 'sugar' hormones like cortisol to help you cope with stress! [learn more](GNS211_U1_T2#GNS211_U1_T2_h4)

question: About how much does a normal pregnant woman's total blood volume increase?

options.A: 5 percent
options.B: 100 percent
options.C: 10 percent
options.D: 50 percent

explanation: Amazing right? The body ramps up blood volume by about half to care for both the mother and the growing baby. That's why iron and fluids are so crucial! [learn more](GNS227_U7_T011#GNS227_U7_T011_h2)

question: At which spinal level is an intrathecal injection usually performed in adults to avoid damaging the spinal cord?

options.A: C1-C2 or C2-C3
options.B: L3-L4 or L4-L5
options.C: T1-T2 or T2-T3
options.D: S1-S2 or S2-S3

explanation: In adults, the spinal cord ends around the L1-L2 vertebra, so punctures are done lower down at lumbar levels to keep the cord safe. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T10#GNS125_U3_T10_h2)

question: Which part of the pelvis serves as the actual passageway for a baby during birth?

options.A: True pelvis
options.B: Ilioc fossa
options.C: Abdominal cavity
options.D: False pelvis

explanation: Spot on! The true pelvis is the lower bony canal that the baby travels through during delivery. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T10#GNS121_U5_T10_h3)

question: Which blood tests are most important to check before a paracentesis to prevent bleeding?

options.A: Serum creatinine and BUN
options.B: Fasting blood glucose level
options.C: Coagulation profile and platelets
options.D: Total white blood cell count

explanation: We always check clotting times and platelets first to make sure the patient won't bleed too much from the needle poke. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T19#GNS221_U2_T19_h3)

question: Why is heavy reliance on out-of-pocket payments a major problem for patients?

options.A: It forces sick families to pay directly at the point of care, often causing poverty
options.B: It prevents the government from collecting taxes
options.C: It makes doctors prescribe too many laboratory tests
options.D: It forces hospitals to close down their administrative offices

explanation: Paying cash directly for every service at the hospital door ruins household finances during emergencies. [learn more](GST322_U4_T2#GST322_U4_T2_h1)

question: What complication can happen if large amounts of plain tap water are used for lavage in young children?

options.A: Instant calcification of leftover food particles inside the gut
options.B: Dangerous drops in blood sodium levels known as hyponatremia
options.C: Sudden spikes in blood pressure throughout the body
options.D: Permanent hardening of the muscular walls of the stomach

explanation: Plain water lacks electrolytes, and when absorbed in large volumes across the stomach lining, it dilutes blood sodium and causes dangerous water intoxication. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T12#GNS212_U1_T12_h7)

question: What is the primary effect of grapefruit juice on certain medications?

options.A: Binding directly to the drug to prevent any absorption
options.B: Inhibiting intestinal enzymes and increasing drug blood levels
options.C: Speeding up kidney excretion to reduce drug effectiveness
options.D: Neutralizing the chemical pH of the drug in the stomach

explanation: Grapefruit juice blocks specific enzymes in the gut, allowing much more medication to enter the bloodstream. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T2#GNS215_U5_T2_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT a barrier to behavioral change in public health?

options.A: Resistance to accepting new health concepts
options.B: Deeply ingrained cultural habits
options.C: Poverty and lack of basic infrastructure
options.D: Guaranteed availability of free local health resources

explanation: You nailed it! Having free and available health resources actually helps people make positive changes—it isn't a barrier at all. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T14#GNS313_U2_T14_h7)

question: What are some common emotional reactions a client might experience after an abortion?

options.A: Uncontrollable happiness and laughter
options.B: Complete physical paralysis
options.C: Relief, sadness, or guilt
options.D: Total loss of memory

explanation: Emotions are complex and vary widely. A client might feel relief, sorrow, or a mixture of many things—and all of these responses can be completely normal. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T007#GNS226_U5_T007_h6)

question: What is the main benefit of pursed-lip breathing for a patient with chronic breathing difficulties?

options.A: It stops the heart from beating too fast during movement
options.B: It keeps airways open longer by creating gentle back-pressure during exhalation
options.C: It forces all the air out of the lungs in a single quick second
options.D: It pumps extra water vapor directly into the stomach lining

explanation: Breathing out through pursed lips creates small back-pressure that stops fragile airways from collapsing too early during exhalation. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T4#GNS212_U2_T4_h6)

question: A shortage of which mineral leads to an enlarged thyroid gland, known as a goiter?

options.A: Iodine
options.B: Calcium
options.C: Iron
options.D: Zinc

explanation: You got it! Iodine helps the thyroid gland make important hormones. Without enough iodine, the thyroid swells up, causing a goiter. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T7#GNS313_U3_T7_h2)

question: Why does the systemic circulation require higher pressure than the pulmonary circulation?

options.A: It has to travel a much longer distance through the whole body
options.B: It must push blood upward against gravity at all times
options.C: It connects directly to the high-pressure kidney filters
options.D: It handles both oxygen and carbon dioxide simultaneously

explanation: Because systemic blood must reach distant organs from head to toe, the left side of the heart generates much higher pressure than the right side. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T12#GNS111_U2_T12_h1)

question: What is a major direct consequence of unsafe abortion resulting from an unintended pregnancy?

options.A: Severe hemorrhage and sepsis
options.B: Sudden adult onset diabetes
options.C: Chronic kidney stone formation
options.D: Permanent loss of eyesight

explanation: Unsafe abortions frequently lead to dangerous complications like severe bleeding and life-threatening infections. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T018#GNS226_U5_T018_h2)

question: A patient taking oral metronidazole complains of stomach upset. What is the best nursing advice?

options.A: Crush the tablets and mix them into a citrus fruit juice
options.B: Double the next dose to compensate for the upset stomach
options.C: Take the medication with food or milk to ease gastric irritation
options.D: Stop taking the medication immediately and discard the remaining pills

explanation: Correct! Metronidazole can be tough on the tummy, but taking it with meals or milk helps soothe the stomach without losing drug power. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T5#GNS223_U3_T5_h5)

question: Why does a low count of CD4+ T cells make a person vulnerable to many different infections?

options.A: CD4+ cells act as master coordinators that signal other immune cells to fight germs.
options.B: CD4+ cells are responsible for carrying oxygen to fighting white cells.
options.C: CD4+ cells physically trap and digest bacteria in the bloodstream.
options.D: CD4+ cells produce thick mucus barriers on skin and mucous membranes.

explanation: Think of CD4+ cells as the generals in an army. Without them giving orders, the rest of the immune defenses don't know when or how to attack germs! [learn more](GST114_U4_T11#GST114_U4_T11_h2)

question: Why is a quick review session important right after finishing a community disaster simulation?

options.A: To identify weaknesses in the plan and discuss areas for improvement
options.B: To officially close down the community health center for repairs
options.C: To fine community members who moved too slowly
options.D: To hand out formal employment contracts to volunteers

explanation: Spot on! Reviewing the drill helps organizers and participants spot problems and fix safety gaps before a real disaster happens. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T10#GNS315_U5_T10_h6)

question: Which of these is completely unsafe when cleaning up a blood spill on a ward floor?

options.A: Applying a chlorine disinfectant solution over the spilled fluid
options.B: Wiping the spill immediately with a dry tissue paper barehanded
options.C: Putting on heavy-duty utility gloves before starting the cleanup
options.D: Using absorbent materials to soak up the liquid before disinfection

explanation: Never touch blood with bare hands! Always use gloves and proper disinfectants to protect yourself from infections. [learn more](GST114_U2_T14#GST114_U2_T14_h6)

question: Which of these tiny germs cannot survive on its own and must enter a living host cell to multiply?

options.A: A virus
options.B: A bacterium
options.C: A fungus
options.D: A parasite

explanation: Viruses are tiny! They lack the internal machinery to reproduce by themselves, so they have to hijack a living host cell to make copies. You've got this! [learn more](GST114_U3_T2#GST114_U3_T2_h1)

question: What does morbidity measure in a community?

options.A: The state of being unhealthy or diseased
options.B: The total number of registered deaths
options.C: The number of new babies born in a year
options.D: The amount of money earned by hospitals

explanation: Morbidity focuses on illness, sickness, and disease prevalence rather than death itself. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T2#GNS313_U4_T2_h4)

question: A clinic notices a sudden drop in teenagers coming in for counseling. What is the best next step?

options.A: Blame the local school teachers for poor student attendance
options.B: Close the clinic permanently and transfer staff to another district
options.C: Increase user fees to attract a wealthier class of patients
options.D: Investigate possible barriers like staff attitude or operating times through youth feedback

explanation: A drop in numbers is a warning sign. Checking in with the youth helps you pinpoint the problem—whether it's bad staff attitude or inconvenient opening hours—so you can fix it! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T48#GNS214_U1_T48_h8)

question: A patient is experiencing acute withdrawal tremors and confusion. Which nursing diagnosis should be your top priority?

options.A: Ineffective Health Maintenance
options.B: Chronic Low Self-Esteem
options.C: Deficient Fluid Volume
options.D: Risk for Injury

explanation: Correct! With tremors and confusion, keeping the patient safe from falls, seizures, and self-harm is always the absolute first priority in nursing care. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T4#GNS313_U3_T4_h6)

question: Which health condition is directly caused by severe protein deficiency linked to poor dietary practices?

options.A: Type 2 diabetes
options.B: Hypertension
options.C: Kwashiorkor
options.D: Peptic ulcer disease

explanation: Kwashiorkor is a severe form of malnutrition caused by lack of protein, often seen when children are fed only starchy foods because of taboos. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T9#GNS225_U6_T9_h5)

question: A nurse manager wants to check the exact number of patient falls on the ward last year. What type of study is this?

options.A: Descriptive research
options.B: Exploratory research
options.C: Experimental laboratory research
options.D: Basic research

explanation: Exactly! Descriptive research simply counts and describes characteristics or events, like keeping track of how many patient falls occurred. [learn more](GNS217_U1_T4#GNS217_U1_T4_h2)

question: What is the bright triangular light reflex seen on a normal tympanic membrane called?

options.A: The umbo flare
options.B: The malleus reflection
options.C: The annular ring
options.D: The cone of light

explanation: The cone of light is a normal light reflection bouncing off the concave surface of the healthy eardrum. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T3#GNS221_U2_T3_h6)

question: What is a main characteristic of primary health care?

options.A: It is delivered solely by medical specialists inside tertiary hospitals
options.B: It is restricted only to wealthy individuals with private health insurance
options.C: It provides universally accessible and affordable care to the community
options.D: It focuses exclusively on expensive surgical procedures in capital cities

explanation: Primary health care is designed to be universally accessible, affordable, and acceptable to all members of the community. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T6#GNS225_U1_T6_h6)

question: How would you explain 'psychological resilience' in everyday clinical practice?

options.A: The ability to completely avoid all stressful events in life
options.B: A permanent immunity to developing any form of anxiety or sadness
options.C: The capacity to recover and adapt when facing major life hardships
options.D: A physical condition where the brain ignores emotional pain entirely

explanation: Spot on! Resilience isn't about dodging stress—it's about bending without breaking and bouncing back when life knocks you down. [learn more](GNS314_U6_T2#GNS314_U6_T2_h6)

question: Why do doctors frequently order sputum tests for patients in Nigeria who have a long-term cough and breathlessness?

options.A: To evaluate electrical activity in the heart
options.B: To check for acid-fast bacilli and diagnose tuberculosis
options.C: To identify electrolyte imbalances in the kidneys
options.D: To measure the exact haemoglobin concentration

explanation: Because tuberculosis is common around us, checking sputum for TB bacteria is a standard and life-saving step in patient care. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T13#GNS123_U3_T13_h5)

question: What emotional reaction do patients very commonly experience right after losing a limb?

options.A: Indifference to physical changes
options.B: Grief and a sense of loss
options.C: Complete memory loss
options.D: Immediate joyful acceptance

explanation: Losing a body part is a huge life change. Patients go through a normal grieving process, and it's our job to support them with empathy. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T12#GNS324_U4_T12_h7)

question: Which health issue is closely linked to heavy metal exposure from bad toxic waste disposal?

options.A: Neurological damage
options.B: Seasonal allergies
options.C: Vision improvement
options.D: Muscle hypertrophy

explanation: That's correct! Toxic metals like lead and mercury attack the nervous system, leading to serious brain and developmental issues. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T18#GNS122_U3_T18_h6)

question: What is a common research duty for a bedside staff nurse?

options.A: Collecting data and identifying study participants
options.B: Funding major multi-center clinical drug trials
options.C: Writing national health policy legislation
options.D: Publishing textbooks for medical schools

explanation: Bedside nurses are closest to patients, making them well-suited to spot eligible participants and gather accurate clinical data. [learn more](GNS217_U2_T5#GNS217_U2_T5_h2)

question: Why are good learning experiences so important for you as a nursing student?

options.A: They eliminate the need for any written nursing examinations
options.B: They help connect classroom theory to real patient care realities
options.C: They shorten the overall duration of the nursing training program
options.D: They guarantee that students never make clinical errors on the ward

explanation: They bridge the gap between what you read in your textbooks and what you actually see and do at the bedside. Great for building your confidence! [learn more](GST321_U8_T5#GST321_U8_T5_h1)

question: Why is treating a degenerative illness very different from treating a sudden bacterial infection?

options.A: Medications for degenerative conditions never have side effects
options.B: Infection drugs kill the invading germs, while degenerative drugs manage long-term loss
options.C: Infections are genetic, while degenerative diseases are caught from other people
options.D: Infections need lifelong management while degenerative diseases need short antibiotics

explanation: Spot on! An antibiotic can knock out an infection completely, but chronic degenerative conditions need ongoing care because the body's tissues are slowly breaking down over time. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T19#GNS222_U4_T19_h1)

question: Which part of the body is directly injured during the practice of FGM?

options.A: Lower urinary bladder wall
options.B: External female genitalia
options.C: Internal reproductive ovaries
options.D: Major pelvic floor bones

explanation: You got it! FGM involves cutting or altering the external female genital structures. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T4#GNS312_U1_T4_h1)

question: What is the most important first step when assessing a newly met street child?

options.A: Building trust through a non-judgmental and patient approach
options.B: Documenting their home address for official taxation
options.C: Immediately calling law enforcement to detain the minor
options.D: Insisting on immediate blood draws for laboratory tests

explanation: Brilliant nursing logic! Because these kids are used to being mistreated, you have to win their trust before they will let you help them. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T3#GNS225_U5_T3_h6)

question: Within how many days of life is ophthalmia neonatorum typically diagnosed in a newborn?

options.A: Within the first twenty-eight days of life
options.B: Only during the first forty-eight hours
options.C: After six weeks of postnatal development
options.D: Between two and three months of age

explanation: You've got this! Ophthalmia neonatorum is simply eye inflammation that shows up during the first 28 days of a baby's life. Keep up the great studying! [learn more](GNS226_U3_T019#GNS226_U3_T019_h1)

question: What is the very first thing you should do when preparing a client for a family planning referral?

options.A: Send the client immediately to the hospital gate
options.B: Administer a stat dose of an emergency contraceptive
options.C: Write the referral form without speaking to the client
options.D: Establish rapport and create a confidential environment

explanation: Trust is everything in nursing. Welcoming the client warmly and ensuring privacy makes them comfortable to share and listen. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T6#GNS225_U3_T6_h5)

question: You notice a discharged stroke patient is confined to an upstairs room with no wheelchair access. What should you do?

options.A: Advise the family to keep the patient upstairs permanently.
options.B: Assess home modifications and refer the family to local social or disability support services.
options.C: Demand that the local government rebuild the entire house immediately.
options.D: Ignore the situation since the patient is already discharged from the hospital.

explanation: Spotting this barrier is great nursing observation. Your next step is to guide the family with practical advice and connect them to available support. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T16#GNS225_U5_T16_h7)

question: Why is obstructed labor more common among very young mothers?

options.A: Cephalopelvic disproportion caused by an immature pelvis
options.B: Premature hardening of the fetal cranial bones
options.C: Excessive physical exercise during the third trimester
options.D: Over-consumption of dietary iron during the first trimester

explanation: Spot on! Because a young girl's pelvis is still growing, it might be too small for the baby's head to pass through easily. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T8#GNS312_U3_T8_h4)

question: How do we view sleep in modern physiology?

options.A: An active, organized physiological state
options.B: A purely psychological phenomenon
options.C: A complete shutdown of brain activity
options.D: A passive absence of wakefulness

explanation: You might think the brain switches off at night, but sleep is actually a busy, organized state managed by specific brain networks. Great job keeping up with your physiology! [learn more](GNS211_U3_T17#GNS211_U3_T17_h1)

question: Which of these is NOT a common sign of family dysfunction or distress?

options.A: Young children forced into premature caregiving roles
options.B: Open, respectful communication and shared problem-solving
options.C: Unresolved domestic violence and persistent household conflict
options.D: Severe social isolation from neighbors

explanation: Open communication and teamwork are signs of a healthy, happy family, not a dysfunctional one! [learn more](GNS124_U2_T3#GNS124_U2_T3_h6)

question: Which type of mental ability actually tends to stay stable or even improve as people grow older?

options.A: Physical reaction speed during sudden emergency events
options.B: Crystallized intelligence based on accumulated life experience
options.C: Short-term working memory for complex math equations
options.D: Immediate recall of random, unrelated lists of numbers

explanation: Wisdom comes with age! Crystallized intelligence relies on stored knowledge and life experience, which stays strong or even grows as people get older. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T2#GNS324_U3_T2_h3)

question: Which blood test is commonly checked to assess a patient's nutrition before surgery?

options.A: Serum albumin
options.B: Red blood cell count
options.C: Blood glucose
options.D: Platelet count

explanation: You got it! Serum albumin is a classic protein marker we use to check a surgical patient's nutritional reserves. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T009#GNS227_U7_T009_h2)

question: Why do we track urine output after a patient suffers a severe allergic reaction?

options.A: To check for a urinary tract infection
options.B: To measure how much drug is left in the body
options.C: To check if the patient drank enough water
options.D: To see if the kidneys are getting enough blood flow

explanation: Kidneys need good blood pressure to make urine. Tracking output is a clever way to check if vital organs are getting enough blood. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T4#GNS215_U5_T4_h6)

question: Which eye condition usually damages side vision first due to a buildup of pressure inside the eyeball?

options.A: Glaucoma
options.B: Diabetic retinopathy
options.C: Macular degeneration
options.D: Cataracts

explanation: Glaucoma happens when pressure builds up inside the eye, slowly damaging the optic nerve. It usually starts by affecting the outer or side vision first. You've got this! [learn more](GNS324_U4_T8#GNS324_U4_T8_h2)

question: A patient develops sudden chest pain and low blood pressure right after getting a central line placed in their neck. What likely happened?

options.A: An infection of the lungs starting in the bronchi
options.B: Iatrogenic cardiac perforation or tamponade
options.C: A severe allergic reaction to the skin cleanser
options.D: A spontaneous heart attack unrelated to the procedure

explanation: Medical procedures like central line placements carry a small risk of accidentally poking the heart or nearby vessels, leading to bleeding around the heart (tamponade). Don't worry, you'll master these procedural complications in no time! [learn more](GNS213_U1_T9#GNS213_U1_T9_h3)

question: Which of these is a classic example of primary disease prevention?

options.A: Screening adults for high blood pressure at a clinic
options.B: Treating a patient with active tuberculosis
options.C: Providing physical therapy after a stroke
options.D: Administering the polio vaccine to an infant

explanation: You nailed it! Primary prevention stops the disease from happening in the first place, and vaccination is the ultimate primary defense. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T90#GNS214_U1_T90_h4)

question: A patient's surgical wound leaks blood onto the ward floor. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Leave the spill to dry before sweeping it up with a broom
options.B: Mop the area quickly with dry paper towels without wearing gloves
options.C: Put on appropriate gloves and apply a chlorine disinfectant solution over the spill
options.D: Call the administrative office to report a building maintenance issue

explanation: Protecting oneself with barriers and disinfecting the fluid immediately prevents the spread of bloodborne germs. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T8#GNS313_U2_T8_h6)

question: A community health nurse is advising local food vendors. Which safe practice should be encouraged the most?

options.A: Using expired canned goods if the metal can looks dusty
options.B: Leaving cooked rice uncovered on a table all afternoon
options.C: Rinsing raw chicken with bare hands in shared community bowls
options.D: Cooling and storing leftover perishable foods promptly

explanation: Quick refrigeration keeps leftovers out of the 'danger zone' where bacteria multiply rapidly. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T011#GNS227_U3_T011_h8)

question: How do association areas differ from sensory and motor areas in the brain?

options.A: They directly connect spinal nerves to peripheral skeletal muscles
options.B: They are located exclusively deep within the brain stem rather than the cortex
options.C: They only function during deep sleep and remain completely inactive while awake
options.D: They deal with complex thoughts and reasoning rather than direct input or output

explanation: Think of association areas as the brain's processing hubs—they bring different pieces of information together for high-level thinking and reasoning! [learn more](GNS211_U3_T10#GNS211_U3_T10_h1)

question: Why do unhealthy (malodaptive) coping strategies backfire in the end?

options.A: They make the body immune to all future stress hormones
options.B: They only offer temporary relief and often create new problems
options.C: They immediately cure physical diseases but ruin mental health
options.D: They cost too much money for ordinary community members

explanation: Hiding behind quick fixes might feel good for a minute, but it usually leaves the original problem untouched while adding fresh troubles. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T6#GNS313_U3_T6_h6)

question: As a nurse researcher, why would you choose to use qualitative interviews?

options.A: To measure exact physiological vital signs over time
options.B: To explore deep human experiences and personal perspectives
options.C: To test new pharmaceutical drugs on large populations
options.D: To calculate statistical averages of hospital stays

explanation: You've got this! Qualitative interviews are all about listening to patients' stories and feelings, rather than just crunching numbers. It's the human side of nursing research! [learn more](GNS224_U1_T24#GNS224_U1_T24_h1)

question: Why is dietary counselling considered a collaborative process rather than just giving a printed diet sheet?

options.A: Printed diet sheets are illegal for nurses to distribute in a hospital
options.B: It replaces the need for any laboratory investigations
options.C: It involves an interactive dialogue and assesses personal eating habits
options.D: Patients are required to cook meals for the entire nursing staff

explanation: Collaboration means working together through conversation to understand the patient's real lifestyle rather than just handing over generic paperwork. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T001#GNS227_U7_T001_h1)

question: When should rehabilitation nursing care ideally begin for a patient with a neurological issue?

options.A: Only after the patient is discharged to a nursing home
options.B: Several months after all acute symptoms have faded away
options.C: As soon as the patient is medically stable, often on day one
options.D: Once the patient asks to start physical therapy exercises

explanation: Early rehab stops stiff joints and contractures before they start, giving the brain the best possible head start on recovery. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T23#GNS222_U3_T23_h8)

question: What special tools do cancer cells use to break through surrounding tissue barriers?

options.A: Matrix metalloproteinases
options.B: Gastric digestive pepsins
options.C: Liver clotting factors
options.D: Insulin receptor enzymes

explanation: MMPs act like little scissors or chemical drills, helping cancer cells chew through the matrix and invade surrounding tissue. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T7#GNS321_U1_T7_h6)

question: Why is tracking data over time with a wearable better than a single blood pressure check at the clinic?

options.A: It prevents nurses from having to manually record any vital signs
options.B: It completely eliminates the need for any laboratory blood tests
options.C: It guarantees that the patient will take all prescribed medications
options.D: It captures daily trends and avoids single-visit anxiety spikes

explanation: Ever get nervous seeing a doctor in a white coat? Wearables show real everyday trends without hospital stress getting in the way. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T11#GNS212_U4_T11_h3)

question: Why is it so helpful to check a patient's diet early on?

options.A: Predicting future genetic mutations in children
options.B: Determining the exact date of hospital discharge
options.C: Detecting nutrient deficiencies before physical signs appear
options.D: Calculating the financial cost of grocery shopping

explanation: Spotting nutrition problems early means you can jump in and help before things get worse. Excellent nursing intuition! [learn more](GNS227_U5_T006#GNS227_U5_T006_h2)

question: Why must a pregnant woman report blurred vision and a terrible headache immediately?

options.A: They mean the mother needs stronger reading glasses
options.B: They are common signs of normal hormonal adjustment
options.C: They show that the baby is moving too much inside
options.D: They indicate severe high blood pressure or pre-eclampsia

explanation: Headaches and changes in vision are classic warning signs of dangerously high blood pressure. Catching pre-eclampsia early saves lives! [learn more](GNS324_U3_T14#GNS324_U3_T14_h4)

question: Why does the World Health Organization (WHO) classify FGM into different types?

options.A: To determine how much financial compensation the family receives
options.B: To predict exactly how many children a woman can safely deliver
options.C: To measure the exact extent of tissue removal and anatomical alteration
options.D: To decide which surgical instruments should be sterilized

explanation: Having a clear classification system helps us document injuries accurately so we can give each patient the right, tailored care. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T3#GNS312_U1_T3_h1)

question: A nurse feels a patient's radial pulse and notices the beats are uneven and spaced irregularly. What is the correct next step?

options.A: Count the pulse for a full sixty seconds
options.B: Assume the reading is wrong and skip charting
options.C: Double a fifteen-second count for speed
options.D: Check the temporal pulse instead right away

explanation: Any irregular pulse must be counted for a full minute to ensure accuracy and catch any missed beats. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T8#GNS111_U2_T8_h4)

question: Why is tetanus considered infectious, but not strictly communicable?

options.A: It spreads through the air rather than direct contact.
options.B: It cannot be treated with any known medications.
options.C: It only affects animals and never human beings.
options.D: It enters the body from the environment and does not spread from person to person.

explanation: Think of it this way: tetanus spores live in the soil and get in through wounds. You cannot catch tetanus directly from a patient lying next to you in the ward! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T87#GNS214_U1_T87_h1)

question: How many sections make up the abdominopelvic quadrant system?
explanation: The abdominopelvic area is split into four quadrants for rapid clinical screening during assessments. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T4#GNS111_U1_T4_h4)

question: How do chronic staff shortages and power cuts impact nursing human factors on a busy ward?

options.A: They increase mental workload and fatigue, raising the risk of errors
options.B: They automatically prevent nurses from working night shifts
options.C: They improve cognitive focus and eliminate all sources of distraction
options.D: They reduce the need for standardized communication tools

explanation: Too much stress and lack of basic resources stretch your physical and mental limits to the breaking point, making mistakes much more likely through no fault of your own. [learn more](GST319_U5_T7#GST319_U5_T7_h7)

question: Why is handing project ownership over to local community members crucial for sustainability?

options.A: So the program continues running even after external funding or staff leave
options.B: So the government can tax the community for health services
options.C: So nobody can be held responsible if the project fails
options.D: So nurses can retire and stop working permanently

explanation: When locals own and lead the initiative, the program survives independently of outside organizations and temporary grants. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T7#GNS314_U4_T7_h8)

question: Which of these is a great example of a positive feedback loop?

options.A: Insulin lowering high blood sugar back to normal
options.B: Parathyroid hormone raising low blood calcium levels
options.C: Oxytocin increasing uterine contractions during labor
options.D: Thyroid hormone stopping pituitary TSH production

explanation: Positive feedback pushes a process further and faster until the goal is met, just like oxytocin intensifying contractions until baby arrives! [learn more](GNS211_U1_T4#GNS211_U1_T4_h5)

question: A nurse asks her current study participants to help her connect with other patients who have the same rare condition. What method is this?

options.A: Systematic sampling
options.B: Snowball sampling
options.C: Cluster sampling
options.D: Stratified sampling

explanation: Brilliant! Just like a snowball rolling down a hill and getting bigger, snowball sampling grows as participants introduce you to their friends. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T14#GNS217_U3_T14_h4)

question: What is the main job of proteins in the human body?

options.A: Regulating the electrical rhythm of the heart muscle cells
options.B: Building and maintaining structural tissues, enzymes, and hormones
options.C: Providing the quickest and most immediate source of daily glucose
options.D: Storing excess chemical energy compactly inside adipose tissue

explanation: Proteins are the ultimate builders and workers. They make up our muscles, skin, and organs, and also act as enzymes and chemical messengers. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T8#GNS121_U1_T8_h5)

question: A patient is brought to the clinic by their adult child and seems a bit confused. What should you make sure to note about their background info?

options.A: The demographic profile using entirely estimated clinical values
options.B: The source of history as a family member rather than the patient
options.C: The child's personal medical history instead of the patient's data
options.D: The patient as an unreliable historian without further explanation

explanation: Spot on! Always write down who gave the information so the next nurse knows whether it came directly from the patient or a family member. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T3#GNS222_U3_T3_h2)

question: A patient has a burn that looks leathery, dry, and white, and they feel no pain when it's touched. How would you chart this?

options.A: Deep partial-thickness burn
options.B: Superficial epidermal burn
options.C: Full-thickness burn
options.D: Superficial partial-thickness burn

explanation: When all skin layers and nerve endings are fried, it's a full-thickness burn. That's why it looks leathery and doesn't hurt to touch—the nerves are gone! You're building great clinical eyes. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T4#GNS213_U5_T4_h2)

question: What exactly is a 'maternal near miss'?

options.A: A baby delivered prematurely who required care in the special care baby unit
options.B: A woman who experiences mild morning sickness throughout her pregnancy
options.C: A woman who nearly died from a pregnancy complication but survived
options.D: A pregnant woman who almost missed her scheduled antenatal care clinic

explanation: A near-miss is when a mother faces a life-threatening crisis but thankfully pulls through, thanks to quick medical help or pure luck. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T013#GNS226_U1_T013_h2)

question: What's the main difference between getting registered as a nurse and having a practicing license?

options.A: Registration applies only to facilities while licensing applies to individuals
options.B: Licensing is managed by federal laws while registration is handled locally
options.C: Licensing is free while registration requires an annual financial payment
options.D: Registration records qualifications while licensing grants legal permission to practice

explanation: Think of registration as entering your name and certificates into the big record book, while your license is the legal go-ahead that lets you step onto the ward and care for patients! [learn more](GST322_U4_T10#GST322_U4_T10_h1)

question: What type of data is best shown using a histogram?

options.A: Categorical survey groups
options.B: Nominal demographic tags
options.C: Unordered text notes
options.D: Continuous numerical data

explanation: Histograms are built for numbers that flow on a continuous scale (like weight or age), unlike bar charts which show separate groups. You've got this! [learn more](GNS217_U4_T9#GNS217_U4_T9_h1)

question: How does confusion or memory loss directly increase a patient's safety risk?

options.A: It causes the ward floors to become slippery
options.B: It makes it hard for the patient to understand safety instructions
options.C: It directly lowers the patient's blood pressure
options.D: It prevents medications from being absorbed properly

explanation: Patients with memory or thinking problems often forget their limits (like needing help to walk), which can lead to falls. Always good to keep an extra eye on them! [learn more](GNS122_U3_T8#GNS122_U3_T8_h2)

question: A nurse is advising a low-risk traveler on where to stay during a 14-day observation period. Which option is most practical and commonly used?

options.A: Intensive care unit isolation room
options.B: Home quarantine with restricted movement
options.C: A high-security prison medical ward
options.D: The outpatient infectious disease clinic

explanation: For low-risk exposures without symptoms, home quarantine is the standard, practical approach to manage large numbers of people. [learn more](GST114_U2_T16#GST114_U2_T16_h3)

question: In a patriarchal family setup, who typically makes the final financial and health decisions?

options.A: The youngest child in the family
options.B: The maternal grandmother alone
options.C: The male head of the household
options.D: The local community traditionalist

explanation: In patriarchal settings, financial and key decision-making power usually rests with the male head. You've got this! [learn more](GNS312_U4_T7#GNS312_U4_T7_h4)

question: What is the primary danger associated with myxedema coma?

options.A: Severe hypoventilation and decreasing mental status
options.B: Unchecked high blood pressure causing cerebral hemorrhage
options.C: Sudden uncontrollable muscle spasms and bone fractures
options.D: Massive fluid overload leading to acute pulmonary edema

explanation: Well done! Myxedema coma slows body systems down so drastically that breathing becomes dangerously shallow or fails altogether. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T10#GNS222_U2_T10_h8)

question: Which section of a proposal summarizes the entire document and is usually written last?

options.A: Budget
options.B: Reference list
options.C: Methodology
options.D: Abstract

explanation: The abstract is a short summary that gives readers a quick overview of the whole proposal. [learn more](GNS224_U3_T1#GNS224_U3_T1_h3)

question: What traditional mindset often drives "son preference" in many households?

options.A: Assuming that female children cannot survive childhood illnesses
options.B: Believing that girls have higher nutritional requirements than boys
options.C: Viewing boys as permanent family heirs while girls are seen as temporary members
options.D: The legal requirement that only males can inherit ancestral land

explanation: It's an old cultural bias where families invest more in boys because they carry the family name, often leaving girls shortchanged. Changing this mindset is part of our community health advocacy work! [learn more](GNS225_U5_T5#GNS225_U5_T5_h3)

question: Which heart rhythm is a life-threatening emergency that requires immediate CPR and defibrillation?

options.A: Atrial fibrillation
options.B: Premature atrial contractions
options.C: Ventricular fibrillation
options.D: Sinus bradycardia

explanation: Ventricular fibrillation (V-fib) is a true medical emergency! The lower chambers just quiver instead of pumping, meaning no blood flows. Quick CPR and a shock are literal lifesavers here. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T3#GNS213_U1_T3_h3)

question: What is the medical term for infective bone disease?

options.A: Osteoarthritis
options.B: Osteoporosis
options.C: Osteomyelitis
options.D: Osteomalacia

explanation: Osteomyelitis is the specific term used to describe an infection and inflammation of the bone and bone marrow. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T17#GNS222_U1_T17_h1)

question: Why must nurses ask patients about their home environment and social support before discharge?

options.A: To find out if the patient's house has modern furniture
options.B: To decide whether the patient should pay cash or use credit
options.C: To ensure the patient has the help needed to manage recovery safely
options.D: To report neighborhood safety issues to the local police

explanation: Understanding home support and living conditions helps nurses plan realistic and safe post-discharge care. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T2#GNS123_U2_T2_h7)

question: In research, what does 'reliability' mean?

options.A: Consistency of the data collection method or instrument
options.B: The total financial cost of purchasing the research equipment
options.C: How fast the researcher can finish interviewing participants
options.D: Whether the tool measures what it is supposed to measure

explanation: Reliability means consistency. If you use the tool again under the same conditions, you get the same steady results. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T15#GNS217_U3_T15_h5)

question: Why do we use standard universal precautions for every single woman admitted to the labor ward?

options.A: Any patient can carry blood-borne infections even if their screening status is unknown
options.B: It saves time by eliminating the need to check laboratory test results
options.C: Pregnant women never develop secondary bacterial infections during birth
options.D: Government regulations only apply infection control to surgical patients

explanation: We treat all body fluids as infectious because in an emergency, we might not know a patient's status yet. Safety first for everyone! [learn more](GNS226_U3_T009#GNS226_U3_T009_h7)

question: What is the most common early sign of testicular cancer?

options.A: Sudden severe pain accompanied by a high fever
options.B: Recurrent urinary tract infections and visible blood
options.C: A painless, firm lump inside the testicle
options.D: Painful swelling of the entire scrotum during walking

explanation: Spot on! Early on, it usually just feels like a painless, hard lump. That is why monthly self-checks are a lifesaver. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T11#GNS311_U1_T11_h5)

question: An elderly patient with slow kidney clearance is given a standard adult dose of a drug cleared by the kidneys. What are they at high risk for?

options.A: Rapid elimination of the drug before it can work
options.B: Drug toxicity due to medication accumulation
options.C: Severe dehydration from overactive liver enzymes
options.D: Complete lack of drug absorption in the stomach

explanation: If the kidneys are sluggish and you give a full dose, the drug lingers and builds up quickly. This can easily lead to dangerous drug toxicity if the dosage isn't adjusted! [learn more](GNS125_U1_T4#GNS125_U1_T4_h8)

question: What dangerous gases or chemicals are released when medical plastics and waste are burned in open drums?

options.A: Oxygen and nitrogen gas
options.B: Carbon and water vapor
options.C: Helium and neon
options.D: Dioxins and furans

explanation: Burning plastics at low temperatures (like in an open drum behind a clinic) creates nasty chemical pollutants called dioxins and furans, which poison the air we breathe. [learn more](GST114_U6_T9#GST114_U6_T9_h5)

question: Which part of a sterile syringe must a nurse avoid touching to maintain proper aseptic technique?

options.A: The inner barrel and the plunger shaft
options.B: The outer colored flange of the syringe
options.C: The paper packaging before it is opened
options.D: The outside plastic wall of the barrel

explanation: Touching parts of the syringe that will contact medication or enter the sterile pathway introduces germs directly into the patient. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T6#GNS122_U3_T6_h4)

question: Which of the following is NOT a known category of teratogenic agents?

options.A: Infectious pathogens
options.B: Normal dietary water
options.C: Prescribed and illicit drugs
options.D: Environmental radiation

explanation: You nailed it! Clean drinking water keeps us healthy, whereas infections, radiation, and certain drugs are well-known teratogens. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T3#GNS121_U6_T3_h7)

question: Which medication class is widely known to cause constipation as a side effect?

options.A: Short-acting diuretics
options.B: Opioid pain relievers
options.C: Inhaled bronchodilators
options.D: Broad-spectrum antibiotics

explanation: Opioids slow down gastrointestinal motility significantly, which frequently leads to stubborn constipation in patients taking them. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T6#GNS212_U1_T6_h2)

question: A patient asks why walking helps reduce swelling in their legs after surgery. What is the nurse's best response?

options.A: Movement opens up tiny pores in your skin to evaporate excess water
options.B: Skeletal muscle contractions squeeze lymph vessels to push fluid upward
options.C: Walking directly increases the pumping strength of your heart
options.D: Walking prevents blood from entering the lower legs entirely

explanation: Because the lymphatic system lacks a heart, skeletal muscle movement is a primary driver for pushing lymph past internal valves. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T13#GNS111_U2_T13_h2)

question: What usually happens when a healthcare facility does not have a clear organisational structure?

options.A: Better coordination among different hospital departments
options.B: Instant improvement in employee satisfaction scores
options.C: Confusion over job roles and delayed decisions
options.D: A sharp increase in the recruitment of new nurses

explanation: Without clear reporting lines, staff get confused about whose job is whose, and simple decisions take forever. A clear structure prevents this headache! [learn more](GST321_U1_T10#GST321_U1_T10_h1)

question: Which hormone surge directly triggers the release of an egg?

options.A: Progesterone
options.B: Follicle-stimulating hormone
options.C: Human chorionic gonadotropin
options.D: Luteinizing hormone

explanation: A sharp spike in luteinizing hormone—famously called the 'LH surge'—is the green light that triggers ovulation! [learn more](GNS121_U5_T7#GNS121_U5_T7_h3)

question: Which of these is NOT a classic sign of localized inflammation checked during wound care?

options.A: Redness and warmth
options.B: Cyanosis and coldness
options.C: Loss of local function
options.D: Swelling and pain

explanation: Spot on! Inflammation brings extra blood, causing redness, heat, swelling, and pain—not coldness and blueness. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T1#GNS123_U4_T1_h8)

question: Which two-hour post-load glucose level indicates impaired glucose tolerance in a non-pregnant adult?

options.A: 70 to 99 mg/dL
options.B: 140 to 199 mg/dL
options.C: 200 mg/dL or higher
options.D: 100 to 125 mg/dL

explanation: A two-hour reading between 140 and 199 mg/dL falls into the prediabetic range known as impaired glucose tolerance. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T20#GNS222_U2_T20_h5)

question: Why is it important to formally retire older, outdated protocols when introducing a new one?

options.A: It clears away mental and physical space so new practices can take root
options.B: It ensures that doctors do not have to write any more prescriptions
options.C: It prevents patients from reading old medical textbooks in the library
options.D: It saves money on printing paper for the hospital administration office

explanation: Stopping old, useless habits prevents confusion and reduces the workload burden on busy nurses. [learn more](GST319_U1_T5#GST319_U1_T5_h6)

question: What is the appropriate action for a general nurse when a patient requires highly specialized medical nutrition therapy for a rare metabolic disease?

options.A: Refer the patient to a registered dietitian or specialist
options.B: Ignore the condition since nutrition is not a nursing concern
options.C: Guess the correct nutrient formula and prescribe it immediately
options.D: Discharge the patient to avoid having to deal with the complexity

explanation: Nurses must recognize their scope of practice and collaborate by referring complex cases to experts like dietitians. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T001#GNS227_U7_T001_h4)

question: What is the main goal of community-wide public declarations to stop FGM?

options.A: Forcing traditional rulers to give up their titles
options.B: Getting direct cash grants from foreign donors
options.C: Removing social pressure by having families agree together to drop the practice
options.D: Registering all villagers into the national health insurance plan

explanation: Correct! Public declarations protect individual families from being ostracized by ensuring everyone agrees to stop cutting at the same time. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T7#GNS312_U1_T7_h4)

question: How do government irrigation projects help boost farming?

options.A: By reducing total dependence on seasonal rainfall for farming
options.B: By lowering the market price of chemical fertilizers
options.C: By giving formal land certificates to rural farmers
options.D: By providing cash loans to farmer groups

explanation: Irrigation gives crops water even during dry seasons, which means farmers can grow food all year round. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T18#GNS214_U1_T18_h2)

question: What fluid do continuous glucose monitors sample to check a patient's sugar levels?

options.A: Epidermal sweat
options.B: Interstitial fluid
options.C: Capillary whole blood
options.D: Venous plasma

explanation: The tiny sensor sits right under the skin, swimming in the fluid surrounding your cells (interstitial fluid) to estimate blood sugar. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T11#GNS212_U4_T11_h2)

question: Why must a patient empty their bladder right before getting a paracentesis?

options.A: To lower the patient's blood pressure safely
options.B: To prevent accidental puncture of the bladder
options.C: To prevent the patient from feeling dizzy
options.D: To make the urine sample easier to collect

explanation: A full bladder gets pushed up and is way too easy to accidentally nick with the needle. Safety first! [learn more](GNS221_U2_T19#GNS221_U2_T19_h4)

question: Why is passive immunity considered temporary?

options.A: Vaccines prevent passive antibodies from staying in the bloodstream
options.B: The immune system destroys the transferred antibodies immediately
options.C: Maternal antibodies are blocked by the infant's stomach acid
options.D: The body does not manufacture its own memory cells or antibodies

explanation: Passive immunity only supplies ready-made antibodies without teaching the host's cells how to make more, so protection fades away. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T8#GNS313_U1_T8_h4)

question: What is a nurse leader's best first move when handling a disagreement between community groups?

options.A: Suspend the health program until everyone calms down
options.B: Report all complaining members to the local police
options.C: Ignore the tension because arguments always resolve themselves
options.D: Listen to all sides and look for common ground

explanation: Active listening and finding shared interests help calm the tension and bring people together. You're building great leadership skills! [learn more](GNS124_U2_T2#GNS124_U2_T2_h6)

question: Which physical health condition is commonly linked to the chronic stress of long-term unemployment?

options.A: Hypertension
options.B: Sickle cell anemia
options.C: Rheumatoid arthritis
options.D: Type 1 Diabetes

explanation: Correct! Ongoing stress from financial worry keeps the body's stress response switched on, which can raise blood pressure over time. Keep up the great work! [learn more](GNS225_U5_T18#GNS225_U5_T18_h2)

question: Which of the following is a primary goal of conducting epidemiological studies?

options.A: Replacing bedside clinical nurses with data entry clerks
options.B: Eliminating the need for patient consent in research trials
options.C: Providing a foundation for public health policy and disease control
options.D: Ensuring that all hospitals maintain identical financial budgets

explanation: Epidemiology isn't just about numbers—it gives health leaders the real-world evidence they need to build strong health policies and stop outbreaks. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T1#GNS313_U1_T1_h4)

question: Why do nurses care about finding the 'central tendency' in research data?

options.A: It proves whether a clinical trial caused a direct physical cure in patients
options.B: It allows nurses to calculate exact medication dosages for critical care patients
options.C: It helps identify the single typical value that represents an entire group of data
options.D: It eliminates all possible human errors made during patient vital sign collection

explanation: Central tendency gives us a representative middle point so we can easily understand what is normal or typical for a specific group of patients or numbers. [learn more](GNS217_U4_T4#GNS217_U4_T4_h1)

question: An antenatal patient complains that her iron pills make her stool dark and cause mild constipation. What is your best nursing advice?

options.A: Instruct her to stop taking the medication immediately and discard the remaining pills
options.B: Explain that dark stools are harmless and suggest increasing fluid and fiber intake
options.C: Tell her to double the dose so her body adjusts faster to the iron
options.D: Refer her urgently to the surgeon for a bowel obstruction evaluation

explanation: Spot on, nurse! Dark stools are completely normal with iron supplements. Reassuring the patient and encouraging water and local vegetables/fiber helps her stick to her treatment without fear. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T020#GNS226_U2_T020_h7)

question: Why should a nurse gently press the inner corner of the eye (punctal occlusion) right after giving eye drops?

options.A: To make the eye produce more fluid
options.B: To clean away sticky discharge
options.C: To keep the medicine from getting into the rest of the body
options.D: To keep the pupil wide open

explanation: Great job! Pressing the tear duct blocks the drop from draining down into the nose and entering the bloodstream, preventing unwanted side effects. [learn more](GNS311_U3_T4#GNS311_U3_T4_h8)

question: Why do we have to be extra careful and double-check our work when giving injections?

options.A: Oral medications require much higher doses than injections.
options.B: Errors can cause rapid and severe harm because absorption is direct.
options.C: Hospital insurance policies mandate double-checking every dose.
options.D: The digestive system neutralizes all injectable substances.

explanation: Spot on! Once a drug is inside the body via injection, you can't take it back out. That's why accuracy is super important. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T15#GNS122_U1_T15_h1)

question: Where do bedside nurses usually spot their first research ideas?

options.A: By reading financial audits of hospital pharmacies
options.B: Through political debates in national assemblies
options.C: Inside historical textbooks written decades ago
options.D: During routine patient care observations and shift routines

explanation: As nurses, we see what happens on the ward every single day. Your daily clinical experiences are a goldmine for research topics! [learn more](GNS217_U3_T3#GNS217_U3_T3_h2)

question: A nurse complains that a new electronic medication system is too confusing and slows her down. What is likely going on?

options.A: An intentional desire to make medication delivery unsafe
options.B: Physical exhaustion caused by a lack of clinical knowledge
options.C: A personal dislike for hospital management and administration
options.D: Fear of incompetence and disruption of her daily routine

explanation: Learning new tech can feel intimidating! It often triggers a fear of looking incompetent while messing up a comfortable workflow. [learn more](GST319_U2_T5#GST319_U2_T5_h2)

question: What term describes the thinning of the cervix during the first stage of labor?

options.A: Engagement
options.B: Effacement
options.C: Extension
options.D: Descent

explanation: Cervical effacement refers to the shortening and thinning of the cervical canal before and during the dilation process. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T50#GNS214_U1_T50_h2)

question: Which skin change is a classic sign of long-term chronic venous insufficiency?

options.A: Shiny, hairless skin with thick toenails on the toes
options.B: Painful black sores right on the tips of the heels
options.C: Pale, cool skin that turns white instantly when lifted
options.D: Brownish skin discoloration and irritation around the ankles

explanation: High pressure in the lower leg veins forces tiny red blood cells to leak out into the skin. When they break down, they leave behind a rusty brown stain called hemosiderin. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T10#GNS213_U1_T10_h4)

question: Why does the scope of standing orders differ between a small health post and a large health center?

options.A: Patients in urban areas refuse to be treated using standard nursing protocols
options.B: Larger health centers do not trust their nurses to use simple treatment protocols
options.C: Government regulations forbid rural clinics from using any form of written guidelines
options.D: Smaller posts have fewer equipment, drugs, and advanced staff available on site

explanation: The scope of a standing order must always match the available resources, diagnostic tools, and staff training level of that specific facility. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T6#GNS124_U6_T6_h3)

question: What is the most severe and life-threatening complication of unchecked blood loss?

options.A: Excessive weight gain
options.B: Chronic high blood pressure
options.C: Temporary skin flushing
options.D: Hypovolemic shock

explanation: Hypovolemic shock occurs when low blood volume prevents adequate oxygen delivery to organs, causing them to shut down. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T4#GNS123_U3_T4_h8)

question: During which weather condition or season do cerebrospinal meningitis outbreaks typically peak in northern Nigeria?

options.A: Throughout heavy coastal rainfall
options.B: During the dry harmattan season
options.C: During periods of extreme flooding
options.D: In the middle of the humid summer

explanation: Dry, dusty harmattan winds irritate the upper respiratory lining, making it easier for bacteria to invade and cause meningitis. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T5#GNS123_U4_T5_h3)

question: Which of these is NOT a typical healthcare financing challenge in developing countries?

options.A: Large informal economic sectors that evade tax collection
options.B: Excessive government funding that exceeds hospital capacity
options.C: Low budgetary allocation to health by national governments
options.D: High reliance on out-of-pocket payments by patients

explanation: Developing countries unfortunately struggle with too little money for health (underfunding), never too much money! [learn more](GST322_U4_T1#GST322_U4_T1_h5)

question: What do we call those little pouch-like segments you see along the length of the colon?

options.A: Haustra
options.B: Lacteals
options.C: Villi
options.D: Plicae circulares

explanation: Haustra are the cute little pocket formations on the colon created by its muscle bands. You're building solid anatomy knowledge! [learn more](GNS121_U1_T4#GNS121_U1_T4_h3)

question: What is a key piece of advice to give a patient who just received praziquantel treatment?

options.A: You must complete a strict 14-day course of tablets to ensure the larvae in your skin die.
options.B: The drug kills adult worms, but you can still get infected again if you swim in contaminated streams.
options.C: You should take the pills on an empty stomach to prevent the drug from dissolving too quickly.
options.D: The medication will immediately reverse any scar tissue already formed in your bladder.

explanation: Praziquantel wipes out the worms currently inside, but it doesn't give you superpowers against future infections. Patient education is our superpower as nurses! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T10#GNS214_U1_T10_h6)

question: What is a major limitation of receiving care in a residential home?

options.A: Inability of nurses to administer any form of liquid medication
options.B: Strict regulations that forbid doctors from visiting private houses
options.C: Mandatory requirement for patients to cook their own hospital meals
options.D: Absence of 24-hour bedside monitoring equipment and immediate emergency teams

explanation: Homes do not possess the constant electronic monitoring and instant backup staff available in hospital units. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T11#GNS324_U1_T11_h5)

question: What happens to digestion when a woman goes into active labour?

options.A: It slows down significantly or stops almost entirely
options.B: It reverses direction, causing constant vomiting
options.C: It remains completely unchanged from normal pre-pregnancy rates
options.D: It speeds up to clear the body for delivery

explanation: The stress and pain of labour naturally put digestion on pause, meaning food stays in the stomach instead of moving along. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T4#GNS121_U7_T4_h6)

question: Which of these is usually one of the very first warning signs that a patient is slipping into shock?

options.A: Restlessness and increased heart rate
options.B: Elevated blood pressure and flushed face
